transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Natalie Chen (Redwood Product) - Liam O'Connor, Sara Gomez, Marco Ruiz, Anya Petrov (Horizon Data)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), quality vs latency tradeoffs, and a proposed pilot on Redwood Dedicated. Customer wants concrete perf numbers for 8k-context LLM use in their support chatbot, plus regression testing plan.

[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. Um, quick intros - I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, Priya is our SE who will run through the Optimize walkthrough and the quantization profiles.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, Liam here, CTO at Horizon Data. We're excited to understand the cost/latency tradeoff on larger context inference, esp for our customer-facing assistant.
[00:28] Priya Shah: Great, thanks Liam. Quick agenda: show INT8 and FP8 profiles, quality-vs-latency charts, demo the Console Optimize suggestions, and discuss pilot scoping. I'll call out caveats for certain model families.
[00:40] Sara Gomez: Quick note - our eval set is heavy on multi-turn, 8K windows and we care about hallucination rates more than micro-token perplexity.
[00:52] Ethan Park: Noted. Marco, you mentioned infra constraints in the signup - anything we should be aware of?
[00:58] Marco Ruiz: Yeah, we run mixed fleets of A100s and some older V100, and we want VPC-only access for the pilot. Also KMS integration is required.
[01:10] Priya Shah: That's fine - Redwood Private or Dedicated can do VPC and KMS. For the benchmark today we'll show hosted numbers and also Dedicated profiles.

[01:28] Priya Shah: Ok walking through slide one - high level: FP8 tends to keep quality near FP16 and gives the best latency improvement for decoder-only families, INT8 gives larger model-size reduction but sometimes needs per-layer calibration for quality-sensitive tasks.
[01:45] (murmur)
[01:50] Priya Shah: Here's a chart from our Optimize tool - you can see p95 latency vs quality delta for a 8k prompt, FP8 is like 10-20% latency down with <1% quality drop on our internal eval, INT8 can be 30-45% faster but quality delta varies by prompt set.
[02:12] Sara Gomez: When you say quality delta, how are you measuring it?
[02:17] Priya Shah: We're using a mix - exact-match on structured extraction tasks, and a QA based F1 for open generation, plus human eval samples. For hallucination we run targeted prompts and measure false assertions count.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: Do you have examples on multi-turn consistency? That's our main failure mode.
[02:36] Priya Shah: Yes, we included a multi-turn eval. In FP8 the multi-turn coherence stayed within 2-3% of FP16; INT8 had a wider spread, some model families showed 6-8% drop. We can send the raw eval CSV.

[03:05] Ethan Park: One thing to flag are autoscaling and batching interactions - INT8 often lets you pack more concurrent requests and reduces GPU mem so throughput wins can be multiplicative, but latency SLOs require careful batching config.
[03:20] Marco Ruiz: Right, our p95 SLO is 350 ms for short queries, but long 8k generations can be a few seconds, we mostly care about p95 for short.
[03:33] Priya Shah: For short queries we tend to recommend FP8 first because it preserves quality and gives latency wins without as much calibration. INT8 is great for cost optimization once you lock prompt set and evals.

[03:58] (sound of keyboard)
[04:05] Priya Shah: Demo time - opening Redwood Console, Optimize -> Profiles. You can see recommended profiles based on your workload scan. Here we have an example profile: model xyz-8k, FP8-optimized kernels, prefix KV cache enabled, smart batching set to 16ms window.
[04:30] Sara Gomez: The console is picking configs automatically? How transparent are the changes?
[04:36] Priya Shah: Yes, Optimize suggests a set of profiles with estimated delta for cost and quality. You can click into each and see the sample evals that were used to estimate quality impact. We also attach raw metrics and a confidence score.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: Confidence score calculation - what goes into that?
[04:55] Priya Shah: It's a heuristic: number of eval prompts, similarity of your prompt distribution to our benchmark, and model family variance. If similarity is low, confidence is lower and we recommend a shadow test.

[05:20] Priya Shah: Switching to the perf spreadsheet - example numbers for 8k context on an A100: FP16 baseline p95 620ms, FP8 p95 520ms, INT8 p95 380ms. Token throughput improved 1.2x for FP8, 1.8x for INT8. Quality delta (human score) FP8 -0.6%, INT8 -3.4% on our mixed eval.
[05:48] Sara Gomez: Those INT8 quality hits are a bit scary. How do we mitigate?
[05:53] Priya Shah: Calibration and per-layer quantization, selective fallback for certain prompt types, and caching hot prefixes. Also we support hybrid profiles - e.g., INT8 for retrieval-heavy paths, FP8 for instruction-heavy generation.
[06:10] Marco Ruiz: Any memory caveats on older V100?
[06:14] Priya Shah: V100 may not have FP8 kernel support so FP8 benefits will be smaller; INT8 still helps but kernel availability varies. We'll include a hardware compatibility table in the docs we send.

[06:33] (brief pause)
[06:40] Priya Shah: Quick note on regressions - Redwood Optimize ties each profile to a regression harness and prompt set; when you deploy a profile we run periodic evals and alert on drift. For pilot we'll set threshold for hallucination and F1 drops.
[06:58] Anya Petrov: Do you keep logs or raw tokens for audits? Compliance is a concern.
[07:04] Ethan Park: We have retention controls and can integrate with customer KMS; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed logs and audit trails. We'll share SOC2 and the retention options.

[07:20] Sara Gomez: Can we run A/B tests on rollouts? We want to test FP8 vs INT8 on a small percentage of traffic.
[07:27] Priya Shah: Yes, rollouts support canary and weighted A/B. You can route by route or by user bucket and collect quality metrics back to our console.

[07:45] Liam O'Connor: Cost question - ballpark cost reduction if we go INT8 on 24/7 traffic?
[07:52] Ethan Park: On average customers see 25-40% cost reduction for inference compute when moving from FP16 baseline to INT8 at scale, but this depends on model size and utilization. FP8 usually sits in the mid 10-20% savings with fewer bells and whistles.

[08:10] (background)
[08:15] Priya Shah: Demoing a quick shadow test setup - we can run your prompt set against FP16, FP8, INT8 overnight and give you a CSV with per-prompt deltas, p95 latency, and resource usage. This is what we recommend before a production switch.
[08:32] Marco Ruiz: That sounds useful - we'll provide the prompt set and a few sample conversations.

[08:45] Sara Gomez: On the safety/regression harness - how many prompts do you recommend for meaningful signal?
[08:52] Priya Shah: Minimum 2k targeted prompts across categories; 5-10k gives good statistical power for most metrics. If you have lower volume we can do stratified sampling and manual review for high-risk categories.

[09:10] (chime)
[09:12] Priya Shah: Quick question from our side - what is your expected timeline and decision criteria?
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: We want a pilot within two weeks and decision in 6 weeks. Criteria: keep hallucination delta <2% on our eval, p95 for short queries <350ms, and cost improvement >20% to justify Dedicated commit.
[09:33] Ethan Park: Great, that lines up with a pilot run and a week-long shadow test. We'll scope cost numbers for Dedicated during pilot.

[09:45] (overlap)
[09:50] Priya Shah: I'll outline a pilot plan: 1) Shadow run on hosted for 48h with your prompt set, 2) 1-week pilot on Dedicated in your VPC with KMS, running FP8 and INT8 profiles, 3) evaluation and go/no-go.

[10:10] Sara Gomez: For the pilot can we limit to a single route - user chat generation - and isolate retrieval separately?
[10:16] Priya Shah: Yes that's best practice. Keep retrieval on FP16 or FP8 while generation experiments with INT8.

[10:28] Liam O'Connor: Any risks for live traffic? We need automatic fallback if quality drops.
[10:33] Priya Shah: We recommend a fallback policy on route level: if confidence drops or latency spikes, route back to FP16 or FP8. Redwood supports automatic fallback and can trigger alerts to Slack.

[10:50] Ethan Park: Ok we're wrapping - I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and a link to the pilot onboarding doc. Priya will share the quantization checklist and the regression harness template.
[11:00] Marco Ruiz: We'll gather prompts and existing p95 data and send to Ethan and Priya.

[11:12] Recap and next steps:
- Ethan: Send INT8/FP8 benchmark spreadsheet and cost model (due 2026-09-12)
- Priya: Share quantization tuning checklist + sample Optimize profile (due 2026-09-13)
- Marco: Provide current latency and token distribution (due 2026-09-15)
- Schedule pilot targeting week of 2026-09-20

[11:35] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone, good session.
[11:38] Ethan Park: Thank you, talk soon.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings and punctuation issues, proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., model family names abbreviated). Links referenced in call: Pilot onboarding doc (link shared in chat), Benchmark spreadsheet (to be sent by Ethan), Quantization guide (to be sent by Priya).
